_comment_intent: Automate the decision, not the runtime.
docs/UPGRADING.md argues that nothing in this stack should update itself:
Postgres major bumps are one-way data-directory migrations, and Dendrite
migrates its own schema forward on boot. An unattended pull is an
unsupervised migration with no backup step and no way back.
But 'update it when you remember' is not a policy either, and the reason
version bumps rot is that testing them is manual. So: this bot proposes,
CI proves with the same preflight a release runs, and a person merges.
Nothing here auto-merges. That is the whole design and it is deliberate.
_comment_lockfile: CI installs with --frozen-lockfile, so a PR that changes package.json
without the lockfile fails at step 1 of preflight. Renovate updates both.

_comment: Off-schedule on purpose. Waiting until Monday to hear about an advisory
is a policy that only works until the week it doesn't.
cloudflared is the only process in the compose file with an
unsolicited path to the internet. It sat on 2024.12.2 for twenty
months while everything else looked fine. Its own PR, always.
Postgres majors are a one-way data-directory migration. Pinned to a
minor, an accidental major refuses to start, which is the good
outcome. A PR is still welcome — it just needs somebody to read
docs/UPGRADING.md before merging it, hence the label.
Dendrite migrates its own schema forward on boot, and the element-hq
fork is in maintenance mode taking security fixes only. Both facts
make a bump here a decision rather than a chore.
One PR for the whole Express move. Its transitive dependencies
(path-to-regexp, qs, body-parser, send, serve-static) are five of the
eight advisories in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md and are meaningless to bump
separately — they arrive with Express or not at all.
The crypto stack moves together or not at all. A matrix-js-sdk that
disagrees with its Rust bindings fails at runtime in the crypto
stage, not at typecheck.
Tauri's Rust and JS halves are one product with two package
managers. Splitting them produces a desktop that typechecks and does
not build — which is exactly how v0.6.1's release broke.
Everything with no runtime blast radius, batched weekly so the
interesting PRs above are not buried in them.
